summary: Count the connected components of an undirected graph with n nodes and an edge list.
mainInsight: Build an adjacency list, then run DFS/BFS from every unvisited node; each search covers one component. Alternatively use union-find: start with n components and decrement for each successful union.

approaches.name: DFS/BFS over an adjacency list
approaches.summary: Count the number of searches started.

approaches.name: Union-Find
approaches.summary: components = n; each union of two different roots reduces it by one.
strengths: No graph structure, handles edges as a stream

personalSolution.notes: Optimal in time; union-find is the compact alternative.

options: Start with n; subtract 1 for each union of two different components
Add 1 for every edge processed while scanning the edge list
Count the leaves of the spanning forest after all the unions
Sort the edges by weight, then count the groups that form
cards.answer: Start with n; subtract 1 for each union of two different components
cards.explanation: Each successful merge joins two components into one.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Add 1 for every edge processed while sca: Edges can join components or lie inside one.

promptVariants: Why must isolated nodes (no edges) be counted?
How does your loop handle them?
cards.answer: An isolated node is its own component. The loop iterates over all n node labels (not just those appearing in edges), so each unvisited isolated node triggers a (trivial) DFS and increments the count.
cards.explanation: A graph.keys() loop would miss them.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Time complexity (V nodes, E edges): ___
cards.explanation: Building the lists and the traversals are linear.

promptVariants: What are the memory costs of DFS vs union-find?
Compare the memory of DFS with an adjacency list and union-find for counting components.
cards.answer: DFS: O(V + E) for the adjacency list plus O(V) visited and recursion. Union-find: O(V) for the parent array.

promptVariants: What is the answer for n = 5 and edges = []?
What about a single connected chain?
cards.explanation: Without edges every node is alone; a chain connects everything into one component.

incorrectOptionExplanations.0, and 1: There are nodes, so components exist.
